translations.text: The word of the Lord that came to Micah of Moresheth in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
Listen, all you peoples! Pay attention, earth and everything in it! Let the Lord of lords be a witness against you, the Lord from his holy temple.
For look, the Lord is coming out of his place; he will come down and tread on the heights of the earth.
The mountains will melt beneath him, and the valleys will be torn apart, like wax before fire and like water pouring down a slope.
All this is because of Jacob’s wrongdoing and the sins of the house of Israel. What is Jacob’s wrongdoing, if not Samaria? And what is Judah’s sin, if not Jerusalem?
I will make Samaria an open place in the countryside, a place for planting a vineyard. I will gather her stones into a heap and uncover her foundations.

All her carved images will be utterly shattered, and all the things she worships will be burned with fire. I will destroy all her idols, because they were gathered from a prostitute’s wages, and to a prostitute’s wages they will return.
Because of these things, mourn and wail! Walk barefoot and naked, and make a lament like a jackal and mourn like an ostrich.
For her wound is painful, and it has reached Judah. It has come right up to the gate of my people, to Jerusalem.
Do not rejoice in Gath, and do not weep at all. In the houses of dust, roll yourselves in the dust.
Prepare yourself, inhabitant of Shaphir, in nakedness. The inhabitant of Zaanan went out and was not ashamed. The lamentation of Beth-ezel will take its wound from you.
For the inhabitant of Maroth became sick with longing for good, because disaster came down from the Lord upon the gates of Jerusalem.
The inhabitant of Lachish harnessed chariots with swift horses. She was the beginning of sin for the daughter of Zion, because Israel’s sins were found in you.
Therefore you will give up the inheritance of Gath. Houses of emptiness have become emptiness for the kings of Israel.
Bring heirs to yourself again, inhabitant of Mareshah! The glory of Israel will rise forever.
Make yourself bald and cut off your hair for the children you have pampered. Make your baldness as extensive as an eagle’s, because they have been taken captive away from you.
Woe to those who plan wrongdoing and devise evil on their beds! They rise early in the morning and carry out what they planned, and they lift their hands toward God.
They covet fields and houses and seize them by force. They defraud a man of his property and his inheritance.

Because of these things, this is what the Lord God says: Look, I am planning disaster against this family, from which you will not lift your necks. You will not walk upright with pride, because it is a time of disaster.

On that day someone will take up a taunt against you and sing a mournful lament, saying, “A plunderer will plunder us! He will divide my people’s portion equally, and there is no one to restore our fields fairly.”
Therefore you will have no one in the Lord’s assembly to measure with a line and distribute portions by lot.
Do not shed tears, and do not weep over these things, so that disgrace does not overtake you.
It is said of the house of Jacob that it angered the Spirit of the Lord by these practices of its. Look, my words do good to the one who walks uprightly.
Yesterday my people stood like a thief against his peace. You strip off his skin to take away his hope and turn back war.
You drive the women of my people out of the homes where they lived in comfort, and you take glory away from their children forever.
Get up and go, for this is not a resting place. Because of its uncleanness it will bring destruction, and its destruction will be severe.
A man walking in the spirit falsely and deceitfully says, “I will preach to you about wine and drunkenness,” and you will be among this people’s preachers [?].

I will certainly gather all of you, Jacob. I will certainly bring together the remnant of Israel. I will make them like sheep in distress, like a flock within its resting place, sheltered from people.
The one who breaks through went up before them. He broke open a passage, and they passed through and went out through it. Their king passed before them, with the Lord at their head.
And he said: Listen now to these things, leaders of the house of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel! Is it not your duty to know justice?
You hate good and love evil. You tear their skin from them and their flesh from their bones.
They ate the flesh of my people, stripped their skin from them, broke their bones, and threw them in as into a kettle, like meat in a pot.
Then they will cry out to the Lord, but he will not answer them. He will turn his face away from them at that time, because they have made their deeds evil.
This is what the Lord says concerning the prophets who lead my people astray, who bite with their teeth and proclaim peace, but proclaim war against anyone who puts nothing into their mouths:
Therefore you will have night instead of vision, and darkness instead of divination. The sun will set upon the prophets, and the day will grow dark over them.
Those who see visions will be ashamed, and the diviners will be disgraced. They will all cover their lips, because God has not answered them.
But I am filled with the power of the Spirit of the Lord, with justice and courage, to declare to Jacob his wrongdoing and to Israel his sin.
So hear this, leaders of the house of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel, who despise justice and twist everything that is right.
They build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with injustice.

Her leaders judge for bribes, her priests teach for payment, and her prophets practice divination for money. Yet they rely on the Lord and say, “Look, the Lord is among us! No disaster will come upon us.”
Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become a ruin, and the mountain of the house will become a wooded place.
In the last days, the mountain of the Lord’s house will be established at the head of the mountains and raised above the hills, and all the nations will gather to it.

Many nations will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob. He will teach us his ways, and we will walk in his paths.” For the law will go out from Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

It will judge between nations and settle disputes for mighty nations far away. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into sickles. Nation will not raise a sword against nation, and they will no longer learn warfare.
Everyone will sit under their vines and under their fig trees, with no one to frighten them, for the mouth of the mighty Lord has spoken.
For all the nations will walk, each in the name of its god, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and ever.
“On that day,” says the Lord, “I will gather those who are far away and bring near the scattered, those whom I have afflicted.
I will make a remnant of the scattered and a mighty nation of those who are far away.” The Lord will reign over them on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem from now and forever.
But you, tower of the shepherd, dark place of Daughter Zion, your time has arrived, and the former ruler of the kingdom of Daughter Jerusalem is coming.
Now why have you done evil? Is there no king within you, or have your counselors perished, so that pains have seized you like a woman giving birth?

Suffer labor pains and be strong, Daughter Zion, like a woman giving birth. For now you will leave the city and camp in the open country. You will go as far as Babylon, and there you will be rescued. There the Lord will redeem you from the hands of your enemies.
Now many nations will gather against you, those who were saying, “Let Zion be defiled, and let our eyes look upon her.”
But they do not know the Lord’s thoughts or understand his purpose: he has gathered them like ears of grain to the threshing floor.

Rise and thresh them, Daughter Zion, for I will make your horns iron and your hooves bronze. You will crush many nations and devote their possessions to the Lord and their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.
Now you will go out with a troop, daughter of mighty troops that have risen against us and struck the shepherd of Israel on the cheek with a rod.
But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, are small among the thousands of Judah. From you will come a ruler who will rule over Israel, whose origin is from the beginning, from the days of old.
Now he will give them up until the time when the woman in labor gives birth. Then the rest of his brothers will return to the people of Israel.
He will stand and shepherd in the strength of the Lord and in the glory of the name of the Lord his God. They will return, for now he will become great to the ends of the earth.
There will be peace. When the Assyrian comes into our land and tramples our fortresses, we will raise against him seven shepherds and eight leaders of men.
They will devastate the land of Assyria with the sword and the land of Nimrod in his wrath. He will rescue us from the Assyrian, so that he will not enter our land or tread within our borders.
The remnant of Jacob will be among the people, among many nations, like dew from the Lord and like showers upon the grass, which do not wait for a man or linger for a human being.

The remnant of Jacob will be among the people, among many nations, like a lion among the animals of the flock and like a young lion among a flock of sheep, which, when it breaks away and tears apart, crushes, with no one to rescue.
Your hand will be raised against those who hate you, and all your enemies will perish.
On that day, says the Lord, I will destroy your horses from among you and destroy your chariots.
I will destroy the towns of your land and overthrow all your fortresses.
I will remove sorcery from your hands, and you will no longer have mediums.
I will destroy your carved images and your sacred pillars from among you, and you will no longer worship the work of your hands.
I will destroy your plantings from among you and lay waste your cities.
In anger and wrath I will take vengeance on the nations that have not obeyed.
Now hear what the LORD says: Rise and plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.
Hear the LORD’s case, you mountains and depths of the earth’s foundations, for the LORD is bringing a case against his people and rebuking Israel.
My people, what have I done to you? How have I distressed you? Testify against me.
Did I not bring you up from the land of Egypt and redeem you from the house of slavery? I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam ahead of you.
My people, remember, then, what Balak king of Moab plotted against you and what Balaam son of Beor answered him, from Shittim to Gilgal, so that you may know the righteousness of the LORD.
With what shall I come before the LORD and please God Most High? Shall I come before him with whole burnt offerings or with year-old calves?
The LORD takes no pleasure in a thousand rams, nor in vast quantities of oil. If I give my firstborn, it is wrongdoing on my part, and the fruit of my womb is a sin on my soul.
I have shown you, human being, what is beneficial, what the LORD requires of you: to practice justice, to love kindness, and to be ready to follow your God.
The LORD's voice proclaims instruction over the city to those who fear his name. Listen, tribe! Who will testify?
For there is still fire in the house of the wicked, along with treasures of wickedness and an oppressive short measure.
How can they be acquitted with dishonest scales and bags of fraudulent weights?
For her rich people are full of violence, her inhabitants speak lies, and their tongues are deceitful in their mouths.
I too will begin to strike you and destroy you because of your sins.
You will eat but will not be satisfied, and dysentery will be within you. You will overtake but will not rescue, and whatever you rescue I will hand over to the sword.
You will sow but will not reap. You will press olives but will not anoint yourself with oil. You will press wine but will not drink it.

Because you have kept the commands of Omri and all the practices of the house of Ahab, and you have followed their counsels, I have made her an object of horror and her inhabitants an object of hissing. You will bear the disgrace of my people.
Woe to me! I have become like the gleanings of summer, like what is left after the grape harvest. There is no cluster to eat, and my soul longs for the first ripe fruit.
The faithful person has disappeared from the earth, and there is no one upright among humanity. They all lie in ambush, and each hunts his brother to destroy him.
Their hands are ready for evil, and they do no good. The ruler asks for gold, the judge demands a bribe, and the great man speaks the desire of his soul; and they act contemptuously.
Their goodness is like a rag eaten by moths. The day of your watchmen and of your deliverance has come. Now there will be a place of weeping for them.
Do not trust your friends or rely on your relatives. Guard the words of your mouth even from your wife.
For a son dishonors his father, a daughter rises against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. A man’s enemies are the members of his own household.
But I will look to the LORD and wait for God my Savior. My God will hear me.
Do not rejoice over me, my enemy. Though I have fallen, I will rise again. Though I sit in darkness, the LORD gives me light.
I will bear the LORD’s punishment because I have sinned against him, until he pleads my case and secures justice for me. He will bring me out into the light, and I will see his righteousness.
My enemy will see, and shame will cover her who used to say to me, “Where is the LORD your God?” My eyes will look upon her. Now she will be trampled like mud in the streets.
It is a day for rebuilding your walls; it is a day when you will be carried away.
That day of your appointed time will come, from Assyria and from the fortified cities, from Tyre to the River, from sea to sea, and as far as Mount Hor.
The land will become a ruin for its inhabitants because of the fruit of their deeds.
Shepherd your people with your staff, the flock of your inheritance. Let them dwell alone like a flock in the midst of Carmel. Let them graze in Bashan and Gilead as in the days of old.
As in the day when they came out of the land of Egypt, I will show them wonders.
The nations will see and be ashamed of all their might. They will put their hands over their mouths, and their ears will become deaf.
They will lick dust like a snake, and like the moles of the earth they will come trembling from their paths. They will quake before the LORD our God and be afraid.
There is no God like you, who forgives wrongdoing and passes over the sin of the remnant of his inheritance. You do not hold on to anger forever, because you delight in kindness.
He will turn again and have mercy on us. He will gather up all our wrongdoing and throw all our sins into the depths of the sea.
You will show faithfulness to Jacob and kindness to Abraham, as you swore to our ancestors in days long ago.
